title: Great Irish Famine
summary: Potato crop failures beginning in 1845 brought famine to Ireland, which lasted until about 1852. A University College Cork atlas project says it is now widely accepted that a million people died and at least one and a quarter million left, mostly for North America.

uncertainty.note: UCC gives 1845-52; History.com says crops did not fully recover until 1852.

where.modern_name: Island of Ireland (pin is a proxy at the island's approximate centre)
where.historical_name: Ireland, United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland

importance.justification: UCC calls it probably the most pivotal event in modern Irish history, with global reach.

audience_note: Concerns mass starvation, disease and death of a large share of a population.

sources.title: Atlas of the Great Irish Famine 1845-1852
Irish Potato Famine: Date, Cause & Great Hunger

reviewer_note: Pin is a proxy for the whole island from a weak coordinate source; death toll is approximate (History.com says estimates vary). Britannica gives 1845-49 for the crop failures but was not opened.
